_comment: Multiple engage target cycling (#1084): UnitCombat.strike() only ever damages whichever ONE enemy target_enemy currently resolves to, so a MULTIPLE_ENGAGE unit genuinely fighting 2+ distinct adjacent enemy regiments at once used to keep every strike locked onto whichever one it engaged first -- the other sat in FIGHTING state taking zero casualties indefinitely. One player Infantry regiment (team 0, uid 0, 58 soldiers) starts near-stationary and centred; two enemy Infantry regiments (team 1, uid 1 'Holdout North', 20 soldiers, and uid 2 'Holdout East', 24 soldiers) auto-advance on it from different bearings -- one from due south, one from the east-south-east. At tick 8, before either reaches contact, the player selects the unit and issues Ctrl+F2 (Multiple engage). Verified via dump-state.sh: uid 1 reaches contact first (~tick 170) and target_enemy_uid locks onto it (1); both regiments become simultaneously adjacent for a window around tick 320-340, and target_enemy_uid then switches to uid 2 (2) and stays there. uid 1's soldier count drops 20 -> 13 while it's the active target, then holds steady at 13 once the cycle moves on; uid 2's count holds at 24 while untouched, then drops 24 -> 21 across the rest of the clip once it becomes the active target -- both regiments end up damaged instead of only the first one engaged. Driven live through the real SelectionManager by tools/demo/DemoInputRecorder.gd. World coordinates; physics ticks (60/s).
